**Core difference: merge preserve history, rebase rewrite it.**

**Merge**
```
git checkout main
git merge feature
```
Creates merge commit with two parents. Feature commits keep original hashes, original timestamps, original parent. History shows what really happened — branch existed, branch joined. Graph get diamond shapes.

**Rebase**
```
git checkout feature
git rebase main
```
Takes your commits, replays them one-by-one on top of new base. New commits, new hashes — old ones orphaned. History becomes straight line. Looks like you wrote feature after main's latest commit, even though you didn't.

**Conflict handling differ too.** Merge: one conflict resolution, all at once. Rebase: conflict per replayed commit, possibly same conflict many times. Long branch + big divergence = rebase pain. `git rerere` help repeat cases.

**When rebase**
- Your local branch, not pushed. Sync with main before PR: `git rebase main`.
- Cleanup before sharing: `git rebase -i` to squash "wip", "fix typo", "fix fix".
- Team wants linear history — bisect and blame read easier on straight line.
- Pulling: `git pull --rebase` avoid junk merge commits from trivial sync.

**When merge**
- Branch shared with others. Rebase rewrite hashes; their clones diverge, force-push needed, teammates get mess.
- Long-lived branches (release, develop).
- You want record that feature was separate unit of work. Merge commit is that record.
- Conflicts big and messy — resolve once, not per-commit.

**Rule that matter most:** never rebase commits others pulled. Public history rewrite = force-push = everyone's local history broken. Rebase private work, merge public work.

**Common hybrid:** rebase your feature onto main to clean up, then merge with `--no-ff` into main. Linear feature commits plus explicit merge point marking feature boundary. GitHub "Rebase and merge" and "Squash and merge" buttons are variants of this.

**Safety net:** rebase gone wrong recoverable. `git reflog` shows pre-rebase state, `git reset --hard HEAD@{n}` restore. Nothing lost for ~90 days.
